title: RGBAF16 weird bug?
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

40.0.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Other Linux

### Operating System Version

Linux 6.18.7-2-cachyos #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Sat, 24 Jan 2026 21:21:21 +0000 x86_64 GNU/Linux

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

39.3.0

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

On a non HDR monitor it shouldn't be active? I guess.

### Actual Behavior

The monitor I use at my workplace is crappy 60Hz not too old but also not very new.

If i opened the outlook electron web app on the 2nd monitor (so the off monitor) it made:
- The colors weird. Orange and light orangeish looked yellow. Grey was almost black.
- The saturation was weird .. or it was contrast? The white color seemed very 'bright'. If there was a part with white and black text on it ... it became almost unreadable 
- Some other texts also became hardly readable

Downgrading back to 39.3.0 the problem goes away and this was the thing in the changelog that it was color related.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

_No response_

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Found a workaround for this: https://github.com/brave/brave-browser/issues/50027

```ts
if (process.platform === 'linux') {
  app.commandLine.appendSwitch('disable-features', 'WaylandWpColorManagerV1')
}
```

Dunno if this has any side effects on HDR displays but on SDR it fixes the bug with 100% brightness I had.

I did not test it under X11 but given the name of the flag I assume this is only an issue on Wayland. (afaik X11 doesn't even support HDR)
